title: Yara and the Veil
premise: Gideon Pemberton has spent his life speaking to beasts in secret, guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains while the crown's new Veil Edict makes his gift a death sentence. When a hunted child beast-speaker collapses at his door, Gideon is forced into open rebellion, joining a ragged company of the gifted seeking the Veil — a legendary doorway said to lead out of Thornfell, a country that was erased from maps and law a generation ago. Betrayed by the smuggler who raised him and pursued by the Inquisitor Vess, who hunts her own sister among the fugitives, Gideon discovers the Veil demands a life freely given. In the end, Gideon offers himself so the others can pass, but the beasts he has loved all his life refuse the bargain, breaking the Veil open for everyone — at the cost of his gift, leaving him human, voiceless to them, but finally belonging somewhere.
about_author: M. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six years leading mule trains through mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write about borders, beasts, and the people who fall between them, and live somewhere with unreliable weather and excellent dogs.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Tongue
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He guides a contraband run through Thornfell's high passes, negotiating with a suspicious mule and eavesdropping ravens, establishing his gift and its dangers. A crown patrol nearly catches him talking to a wolf. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man fluent in a language that could kill him.

chapters.title: The Edict Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the lowland town of Harrowgate, a crier proclaims the Veil Edict: all beast-speakers must surrender for 'curing' or be hunted. Gideon watches neighbors he's known for years look at each other differently. Emotional beat: the moment home becomes a trap.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. During a storm, a starving girl named Wren scratches at his cabin, fleeing hunters; she speaks to his fire-warmed cat before she speaks to him. Taking her in is a death sentence, and he knows it. Emotional beat: fear giving way to a choice he can't unmake.

chapters.title: What the Ravens Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She recovers and tells how the Inquisitor Vess burned her village's gifted, and mentions rumors of the Veil — a door out of Thornfell. Gideon realizes the ravens have been tracking Vess's riders for days. Emotional beat: hope arriving dressed as rumor.

chapters.title: The Old Teacher's Debt
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He seeks out Maren Ostwick, the disgraced scholar who first taught him control, and finds her keeping a hidden ledger of every gifted person still alive. She agrees to guide them toward the Veil — if Gideon swears to protect the ledger. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, old guilt resurfacing.

chapters.title: Down the Drowned Road
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The three flee along a flooded smuggler's route only Gideon knows, using otters as scouts. Vess's hounds are close behind, and one hound recognizes Gideon's voice. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being hunted by something that understands you.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At a ruined watchtower they meet other fugitives: Tam, a horse-speaker deserter; the twins Ilsa and Brann, who speak to crows; and Sorrel, a bitter woman whose gift killed her brother. The group fractures over whether to trust Gideon. Emotional beat: found family forming against everyone's better judgment.

chapters.title: Vess Takes the Pass
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Vess's POV. She interrogates a captured smuggler and learns Gideon's name, revealing privately that her own sister was a beast-speaker she reported years ago. Her certainty cracks for one page, then hardens. Emotional beat: the antagonist shown as a wound wearing armor.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Ambushed on a scree slope, the group must choose between saving their supplies or a wounded stranger; Sorrel argues to leave him, echoing her past. Gideon overrules her, and the stranger later saves Wren's life. Emotional beat: survival versus conscience, argued in blood and cold.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach the edge of old maps where Thornfell 'officially' ceased to exist, and find villages of the erased living outside law and crown. For one night there is music, food, safety. Emotional beat: a glimpse of belonging that makes everything after hurt more.

chapters.title: The Ledger Betrayed
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Crown soldiers arrive too precisely to be chance; Tam discovers someone copied Maren's ledger pages. Suspicion poisons the camp, and Maren confesses she was forced to keep duplicates under threat. Emotional beat: trust shattering exactly when it matters most.

chapters.title: The Man Who Raised Him
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The betrayer is revealed: Corvin, the smuggler kingpin who taught Gideon the roads, sold the route to Vess for amnesty. Confronted in a river gorge, Corvin offers Gideon a place back inside the law — just leave the girl. Emotional beat: the father-figure revealed as a transaction.

chapters.title: Gorge of Broken Voices
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The escape across the gorge goes wrong; Brann falls, and the crows carry his last words to his twin. The group loses their scouts and half their heart. Emotional beat: grief as the true cost of the road, counted in a sister's silence.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. An ancient bear leads them to a cave of carvings proving the Veil is real — and that it once demanded sacrifice. Maren hides this from the group. Emotional beat: knowledge as burden, the scholar choosing mercy over truth.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Confession
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. On night watch, Sorrel tells Gideon the truth: her gift didn't kill her brother — she let him die to save herself, and the crown's cure would feel like punishment she deserves. Gideon refuses to agree. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered and not yet accepted.

chapters.title: The Trap at Hollow Bridge
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vess springs her trap at the last crossing; Corvin points Gideon out personally. Wren is taken, and Gideon surrenders his knife rather than see her harmed. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness, the hunter holding everything.

chapters.title: Inside the Inquisition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Held in Vess's camp, Wren speaks to the Inquisitor's own horses and learns Vess's sister lives — cured into emptiness, kept like a trophy. Wren plants the seed of doubt in Vess's mind. Emotional beat: a child out-arguing power with the truth.

chapters.title: The Door That Demands
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The fugitives reach the Veil: a seam of light in a cliff face that will open for one life freely given. Maren finally reveals the price, and several offer themselves at once. Emotional beat: love measured in volunteers.

chapters.title: Gideon's Bargain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon secretly trades himself to Vess — his capture in exchange for Wren's release — then walks to the Veil intending to give his life. The beasts of Thornfell gather, refusing the payment, and force the door open for all. Emotional beat: sacrifice interrupted by everything he ever saved.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Gift
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Passing through, Gideon feels the Veil take his gift as toll anyway — the voices of beasts gone silent forever. Vess arrives too late, sees her sister's empty eyes reflected in the freed fugitives, and lets them go. Emotional beat: loss and release in the same breath.

chapters.title: A Country With No Name
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Beyond the Veil, the fugitives find the erased descendants of old Thornfell building something new, outside crown and law. Sorrel finally accepts Gideon's forgiveness; Wren takes his hand when the birds sing and he cannot answer them. Emotional beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: Yara and the Veil
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. Months later, Gideon teaches children the mountains without magic, and a wild mare he once knew stands beside him anyway, choosing him voicelessly. Word comes that the Veil now opens both ways. Emotional beat: belonging earned not by gift, but by choice — and a door left open.
